The excitement came after a new nuclear agreement between Iran and the United States and other countries. This deal is important because it will end Iran's isolation from the rest of the world after many years of strict economic sanctions. Just before midnight on Thursday, Vali Asr street, one of the main roads in Tehran, became like a street party. Car horns were honing. Men were dancing in the middle of the traffic. Some people showed U.S. dollar bills.

According to a court document from Brooklyn, a fourth man, Dilkhayot Kasimov, has been charged in a plot to help terrorists and for some of the men to join ISIS. The document was released on Monday. Kasimov was added to a new legal paper that also charges three other men who were already arrested: Abdurasul Hasanovich Juraboev, Akhror Saidakhmetov, and Abror Habibov. They are charged with two counts of providing support to a foreign terrorist organization. Those three men have pleaded not guilty. It is not clear if Kasimov has been arrested.

On Saturday, North American early risers were rewarded with the third of four lunar eclipses. It was the shortest of the series, but still a nice sight. The moon entered Earth’s shadow completely at 4:58 a.m. Pacific Time (7:58 a.m. Eastern Time). This total lunar eclipse lasted nearly five minutes, which NASA says is the shortest total eclipse of this century. The moon turned a burnt-orange color before, during, and after the eclipse, giving it the "blood moon" name.

Istanbul, Turkey (CNN) – On Tuesday, many people in Turkey were afraid and confused. They asked, “What is happening? Why can’t I use the subway?” One elderly woman, wearing a white headscar and carrying shopping bags, stood outside a closed entrance to a busy subway station. She was one of millions of people affected by the worst power outage in Turkey in over ten years. Dozens of cities lost electricity for several hours. Millions of people were affected, including passengers stuck in stopped trains and subways.

During this Holy Week, let us remember what the Bible says about fair and living wages. Isaiah 58 6 tells us: "This is the kind of fast I want: to break the chains of injustice, to end exploitation in the workplace, to set the oppressed free, and to cancel debts." The McDonald's announcement that the company is going to raise wages for 90,000 of its employees is a significant victory for fast-food cooks and cashiers and those of us who support them. By standing up together, fast-food workers are making it less acceptable for profitable companies like McDonald's to pay wages so low that its workers are boxed into poverty.

The Golden State might soon be about the color of California's lawns. Governor Jerry Brown announced on Wednesday that he is imposing mandatory water restrictions for the first time on residents, businesses, and farms. He ordered cities and towns in the drought-ravaged state to reduce usage by 25%. "We're in a new era," Brown said. "The idea of your nice little green grass getting lots of water every day, that's going to be a thing of the past." The 25% cut in usage amounts to roughly 1.5 million acre-feet of water (an acre foot of water equals about 325,000 gallons) over the next nine months, state officials said.

It is almost time for people in the UK to vote. polling stations are ready to open across the country. This election might change how the government works. The campaign was very short, especially compared to the United States, where candidates spend years preparing. The result could give power to Ed Miliband’s Labour Party, taking it from David Cameron’s Conservative government. Or, leaders might struggle to make deals with smaller parties. We will know the answer when voting ends late on Thursday.

This is the time of year when more than 2 billion Christians around the world are remembering the death and resurrection of Jesus. This Holy Week, we are asking Christians to also remember the many ways that religious extremists have attacked them and others just because of their faith. These attacks include crucifix, beheading, stoning, forced slavery, sexual abuse, human trafficking, harassment, bombing, and forcing people to leave their homes. In light of the tragic killing of Christian college students in Kenya on Thursday, and the ongoing threat against Christians in other nations, this is a time to reflect on these things.

The Washington Post has released emails that are racist and offensive. These emails caused three employees in Ferguson, Missouri, to either quit or be fired. The emails were found during a investigation by the U.S. Department of Justice into racial bias in the city's police and courts. The emails contain offensive comments about President Barack Obama, First Lady Michelle Obama, Muslims, and minorities. The Washington Post obtained the emails on Thursday after asking for them through public records. CNN looked at the emails on Friday. Police Captain Rick Henke and Sergeant were involved.

Two people, including a licensed greyhound trainer, have been arrested in Australia. The arrest happened after police found at least 55 dead dogs dumped in the bush near Queensland. Australian media reported the discovery. The two people, who live in Bundaberg, are a 71-year-old man and a 64-year-old woman. The broadcaster ABC reported that they were charged with one count of illegally possessing a firearm. The woman, who is a licensed trainer, was also charged with obstructing police. Michael Beatty, who speaks for RSPCA Queensland, told ABC that the investigation is still ongoing. The animal rights group is helping Queensland police with their investigation.

Two years ago, Mike Premeau and Kathy Danke started a small business called Memories Gourmet Pizza Co. in their town in Wisconsin. They did well, getting their frozen pizzas—including breakfast pizzas and gluten-free options— into stores in Nichols, an area west of Green Bay. They built a loyal customer base. But this week, all of that was put at risk when people began confusing them with Memories Pizza of Walkerton, Indiana. The latter made national news after its owners said they would refuse to cater a same-sex wedding. People left angry comments on Memories Gourmet Pizza’s Facebook page and called its phone number to protest.

A complete camel skeleton, believed to have been used by Ottoman soldiers during the 17th-century siege of Vienna, was discovered under a cellar in Austria. The bones were found by archaeologists from the University of Veterinary Medicine Vienna (Vetmeduni) while working at a shopping center construction site in Tulln between 2006 and 2007. "The partially dug skeleton was initially suspected to be a large horse or cattle," said archaeozoologist Alfred Galik. "But one look at the cervical vertebrae, the lower jaw and the metacarpal bones immediately revealed that this was a camel."

Andrew Getty, the 47-year-old grandson of J. Paul Getty, died on Tuesday afternoon at his home in Los Angeles. His parents, Ann and Gordon Getty, announced the news. They asked the media and the public to please respect the family's privacy during this difficult time.

Ed Winter, an assistant chief at the Los Angeles County coroner's office, told CNN affiliate KTLA that Getty's death seems to be caused by natural reasons or an accident. Some medicine was found in Getty's home, but investigators do not know if he was taking it or what his medical history was.

We may never fully understand why co-pilot Andreas Lubitz crashed Germanwings Flight 9525 into the French Alps on March 24, which killed everyone on board. The latest report shows that he made the plane’s descent faster. It is scary. As the investigation continues, we will learn more about how much Lubitz hid his mental illness, or how much help he asked for. How much did his depression affect his ability to fly? Should he have quit his job? Should his doctors have warned others? His case brings up big and important questions about people with mental illness and the shame that comes with it.

On April 8, 2015, CNN Student News covered several stories. First, they discussed recent news about the United States and Cuba. Then, they talked about California’s severe drought. They explained that the drought’s effects are increasingly affecting other parts of the country. Next, they mentioned a flu outbreak in Chicago, but clarified that it does not affect humans. Finally, they described a proposed tunnel that would connect Denmark and Germany with an underwater road and train line. The page also provides a transcript of today’s show and a way to request being on the CNN Student News Roll Call. Click here to access the transcript of today’s CNN Student News program.

A man who did not want to give his name was caught because of a tattoo on his neck that said "Gertrude." Kankakee County, Illinois, Sheriff Tim Bukowski said this on Saturday. The man is Kamron Taylor, a 23-year-old convicted murderer who escaped from jail before being arrested in Chicago overnight.

 Authorities across Illinois had been searching for Taylor since early Wednesday. He jumped a correctional officer at the Jerome Combs Detention Center in Kankakee. Then he took the guard's uniform and an SUV and ran away. Surveillance video was the last thing officials saw of Taylor until just before midnight on Friday in Chicago. "They saw a guy that matched the description," Bukowski said.

Prince Harry, who is 30 years old and is finishing his military career, is going to Australia. He arrives on Monday for a four-week visit. The Australian military said he will work and live with soldiers in Sydney, Darwin, and Perth. A spokesman said Harry has already spent time with Australian troops several times during his 10 years in the military.

The Florida Attorney General’s office announced on Thursday that two corrections officers and one former officer trainee have been charged with plotting to kill a former inmate who was about to be released. These men used to work as guards in Florida prisons, but they are now the ones in jail.

 According to court documents, the men are Thomas Jordan Driver, 25; David Elliot Moran, 47; and Charles Thomas Newcomb, 42. An FBI informant who was undercover in a branch of the Ku Klux Klan called the Traditional American Knights of the Ku Klux Klan met with them. Driver said he had fought with the inmate and that he and Moran wanted the inmate dead, "six feet under."

Lausanne, Switzerland (CNN) – A series of intense negotiations concluded on Thursday in Lausanne. The P5+1, a group of world powers, reached a framework agreement with Iran regarding its nuclear program. The success of this agreement is still uncertain. The parties have until the end of June to finalize the details and put the plan into writing. However, these talks were historic, especially for the U.S-Iranian relationship, which has otherwise been frozen. However, this does not mean that they were glamorous. In fact, the negotiations this week provided a modern demonstration of diplomacy at its best, but also at its most hectic.

On Monday morning, an homemade bomb exploded near a United Nations vehicle in Garowe, a city in northeastern Somalia. The explosion killed six people, including four aid workers from UNICEF, the United Nations children’s agency. Somalia’s President called the attack, which happened around 8 a.m. in the administrative capital of the Puntland region, “an attack against the future of our country.” Al-Shabaab, a terrorist group, claimed responsibility for the attack, according to the United Nations Assistance Mission in Somalia. This incident follows a separate attack on Sunday, where three African Union soldiers died in an ambush in Somalia’s Lower Shabelle region.

Prince Harry of Britain arrived in Australia on Monday. He will stay there for four weeks to work with the Australian military. Before starting his duty, the 30-year-old prince visited the Australian War Memorial in Canberra, the capital city. He paid his respects at the Tomb of the Unknown Australian Soldier. A crowd of people gathered outside the memorial. Some took photos of the prince, while one boy held a sign celebrating the prince's red hair that said, "Red Heads Rule!" During his time in Australia, Harry will work and live alongside colleagues in the Australian Army in several regments in Sydney, Darwin, and Perth, the Australian Defence Forces said last week.

Australia, a close ally of the United States, has agreed to share some intelligence with Iran. Australian Foreign Minister Julie Bishop described the agreement as " informal" and said its main goal is to track Australians who travel to Iraq to fight for ISIS. However, one Australian lawmaker reportedly called the move " "dancing with the devil." Over the weekend, Bishop became the first Australian government minister to visit Iran in 12 years, meeting with President Hassan Rouhani. The intelligence-sharing deal was announced in an interview released Monday that Bishop gave to the Australian Broadcasting Corporation while in Tehran.

Initial tests on the flight data recorder, which is called the "black box," show that co-pilot Andreas Lubitz intentionally made the plane go down faster. The French air accident investigation agency, the BEA, made this announcement. The black box was found on Thursday by recovery teams. These teams had been searching for days in the French Alps, where the Germanwings Flight 9525 crashed on March 24. The BEA said on Friday that its teams started looking at the contents of the black box right away.

After a 110-day chase across the ocean, the crew of a suspected po-fishing boat was rescued by conservationists who had been following them. The environmental group Sea Shepherd had been tracking the boat, named the Thunder, since their ship, the Bob Barker, found it in the Southern Ocean months ago. The Thunder is wanted by Interpol for suspected fraud and fisheries-related crimes. The chase ended early Monday in the Gulf of Guinea, off the coast of west Africa, when the Bob Barker received a distress call from the Thunder.

16-year-old Jason Zobott goes to Huntley High School in suburban Chicago at 7:30 a.m., just like other students. But what he does after that is different. Jason is part of a special program at the school that mixes online learning with regular classroom teaching. One third of the school’s 2,700 students are in this program. By 215, the school wants most students to join it. Jason, who is a top student and does many activities outside of school, says, “The online work is easy for me to do. I can learn by myself.”

Days after a terrible attack by Al-Shabaab in Garissa, Kenya, launched air strikes against the terrorist group in Somalia. A military source confirmed this. The source said the strikes were not revenge for last week’s massacre at Garissa University College, which killed nearly 150 people. “The latest attack on Al-Shabaab bases by the Kenyan military is part of the ongoing operations that started in 211. It is not a retaliation to the Garissa attack. The operation has been ongoing,” the military source said on Monday. It is common for Kenyan military sources not to give their names to media.

Pope Francis gave a traditional speech after Easter Mass. He reminded the world that the Vatican is its own country and that he acts as a moral leader. He spoke about the suffering of people in current wars and asked for an end to violence everywhere. He specifically asked for the fighting in Iraq and Syria to stop and for help to reach those who need it. "May the international community not stand by before the immense humanitarian tragedy unfolding in these countries and the drama of the numerous refugees," he said in his "urbi et orbi" address, Latin for "to the city (Rome) and to the world."

On Wednesday afternoon, Duke University students and teachers marched together, chanting, “We are not afraid. We stand together.” This happened after a rope noose was found hanging from a tree on the campus. Duke officials asked anyone who knows about the noose to call campus police. The noose was discovered near a student center at 2 a.m. Photos of the noose were shared on social media, which made the community very angry. Hundreds of people gathered on the steps of Duke Chapel, which is close to where the noose was found, for a meeting. Someone said, “You came here because you want to say with me, ‘This is not the Duke we will accept. This is not the Duke we want. This is not the Duke we are here to experience.’”

Muhanad Mahmoud Al Farekh, a 29 U.S. citizen who has alleged ties to al Qaeda, appeared in court on Thursday. He did not enter a plea to charges of conspiring to provide material support to terrorists. Al Farekh was deported from Pakistan to the United States. According to a complaint unsealed in U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of New York in Brooklyn, he is accused of plotting to fight against American forces abroad. CNN counterterrorism analyst Philip Mudd said, "This is news for celebration."

The Saudi state news agency reported that a Saudi border guard was killed in a gunfight with militants in Yemen this week. This is the first known death of a Saudi soldier since Saudi Arabia started air attacks on rebels in Yemen.

The fighting happened on Wednesday night in the Asir region of southwestern Saudi Arabia. militants in the mountains on the Yemen side fired at Saudi border guards, who then fired back. The guard, identified as Cpl. Salman Ali Yahya al-Maliki, was killed. Ten other people were hurt, but their injuries are not life-threatening.

I felt nervous about going to the Al Marmoum camel race in Dubai. because I am the only Gulf national on the CNN team. people expect me to know about camel racing, which is an old tradition in this area. Even though I tried to wear a kandora, which is traditional clothing in the United Arab Emirates, I still feel like an outsider because I have modern views. A friendly farm owner took us into the majlis, which is a meeting place. The camel owners were gathering there. The large room looked like a fancy theater. The owners sat on the floor eating a traditional Arabic dish called a'aish, which is made of fish and rice. They talked loudly and excitedly.

Havana, Cuba (CNN) – Charlie Hill sits in a dark bar on a bright, sunny day in Havana. "Hey man," he says, his voice rough from smoking. He nods, as if he knows you’ve been looking for him. But many people have been looking for Charlie Hill for a long time. For 43 years, Cuba has protected Hill from being charged with killing a New Mexico police officer and hijating a plane to Havana. Hill, now 65, decided to give CNN an interview after we spent two years trying to reach him. He wants to talk about how he is now considering leaving his safe haven and returning to the United States for the first time.

On April 2, 2015, CNN Student News reported that Yemen, a unstable country in the Middle East, might become a battleground for a proxy war. The show explained why Yemen is a major global concern. Also, the program covered the history of April Fool's Day, explained how a 1100-year-old recipe might help fight a modern superbug, and highlighted a woman helping children improve their lives. The webpage provided the transcript of the show and a way to ask to be on the CNN Student News Roll Call.

On April 3, 2015, CNN Student News covers international news from Switzerland, Kenya, and the Pacific Ocean. It also reports on California’s severe drought, which is forcing many residents and businesses to reduce their water use. The program discusses two global religious holidays being celebrated this weekend and examines two topics related to U.S. National Parks. The full transcript is available on the page, and students can also request to appear on the CNN Student News Roll Call.

Misao Okawa, who was recognized by Guinness World Records as the oldest person in the world, has died at the age of 117. She passed on Wednesday morning in Osaka, Japan, Tadahi Uchimura, a local official, told CNN. She leaves behind three children, four grandchildren, and six great-grandchildren. Okawa was born on March 5, 1898. Her family ran a kimono shop in Osaka, Satoshi Yoshioka, an employee at the nursing home where she has lived since 1997, told CNN. "She was a kind person and loved to eat a lot. Her favorite food was sushi and udon noodles," Yoshioka said. "She ate a lot of cake for her birthday last March 5."

Documents obtained by CNN show that the Missouri National Guard, as they were preparing to deploy to Ferguson, Missouri, to help stop the sporri protests that happened last year, used highly militarized language such as "enemy forces" and "adversaries" to describe the protesters. The guard was sent to Ferguson to support law enforcement officers, who many community leaders and civil rights activists accused of using excessive force and inflaming an already tense situation in protests that flared sporri from August through the end of the year.

On Tuesday, gunmen attacked the Somali education ministry in Mogadishu, the capital of Somalia. The attack started with a suicide car bomb that exploded at the entrance of the two-story building. Five gunmen then went inside and shot people.

The attack killed at least 12 people and injured 16 others. Al-Shabaab, an Islamist militant group, claimed responsibility for the attack. Abu Musab, a spokesman for the group, said they were responsible. Mohamed Yusuf, a spokesman for the Somali National Security Ministry, described how the attack began.

Gregory Margolin, now 87, fought in World War II as a 16-year-old Jewish soldier in the Soviet Red Army. He fought against the Nazis while his family fled. Margolin says he did not reveal that he was Jewish, but it did not matter because people were being killed all around him. This year, in Ukraine, he found himself surrounded by war again. Margolin was a sniper who became an army commander. His old uniform still has medals from his military service. His granddaughter, Liora, still marvels at his war stories. She is amazed that he survived.

365 days have gone by since more than 200 Nigerian schoolgirls were taken from their dormitory at night in Chibok, northeastern Nigeria. They are still missing. The Nigerian government and the rest of the world have allowed this to happen. We should all feel ashamed. It is shameful that fan criminals can harm young girls without being punished. It is also shameful that people quickly forget about terrible crimes like this.

Norway is becoming the first country in the world to stop using FM radio. In two years, the country will completely switch to digital radio. This does not mean people will lose access to radio programs. Instead, listeners will use digital technology to listen.

Many Norpeople have already made the switch. The country has a population of about 5 million people. On traditional FM radio, there are only five stations available. However, on the Digital Audio Broadcasting network, there are four times as many stations. According to Culture Minister Thorhild Widvey, half of the country already listens to radio on digital.

Everyone is excited about a good comeback story, especially when it involves a dinosaur. A new study suggests that the Brontosaurus should have its own name again. For over a century, science books had removed the Brontosaurus from the list of dinosaurs.

O.C Marsh first named the Brontosaurus in 1879. He received 5 crates of bones found at Como Bluff, Wyoming, according to the Yale Peabody Museum of Natural History. The dinosaur was similar to the Apatosaurus, which was discovered a couple of years before, but not as large. Marsh named the dinosaur "Brontosaurus," which means "th thunder lizard."

Al Qaeda has offered a reward of 2 kilograms of gold (about $774,000) for anyone who kills or captures two prominent Shia Muslim leaders in Yemen. The group, known as Al Qaeda in the Arabian Peninsula (AQAP), made the offer in an online news release and wanted poster. The two targets are Houthi leader Abdelmalik Bedrudin Al-Houthi, who led rebels that took Yemen’s capital, and former Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh. AQAP called them “the two heads of evil.” AQAP is one of many groups fighting to control Yemen.

Doug Hughes, a 61-year-old postal worker from Florida, wrote about his plans on a website called thedemocracyclub.org before landing his gyrocopter on the Capitol lawn on Wednesday. He said his goal was to expose corruption in Washington, D.C., and to offer solutions to government corruption. The 61-year-old Florida postal worker wrote in an online post titled "Your Pilot" that his flight was not a secret. He said that he sent an email to info@barackobama.com before he took off. The letter was meant to convince the people in charge of the Capitol that he was not a threat and that shooting him down would be more trouble than letting him deliver his letters to Congress.

The problems for Rio de Janeiro before the 2016 Olympics continue. many dead fish were found in the Rodrigo de Freitas lagoon. There is just over a year left before the city hosts the rowing and canoe events for the Games. Rio de Janeiro’s legislative assembly started an investigation on Monday. They want to find out why the fish died in the lagoon and in other lakes and bays in the state. This problem has happened in those places too. The group will work with the State Environmental Institute (INEA) and the State Environment Secretariat.

Anthony Ray Hinton is 58 years old. But he is just now getting used to the free world. Small things, like using a fork, going out at night, and sleeping without someone watching him, are all new to him. He spent nearly 30 years on death row in Alabama. Until last week, when his murder convictions were dropped, and he walked out of a county jail in Birmingham. “I have to pinch myself to tell myself that I’m free,” he told CNN’s Brooke Baldwin on Friday. “It’s going to take a little time, but I’ll get used to it.” Hinton had to get used to much worse. For 30 years, he spent most of his time locked in a 5-by-7 cell.

After the UK election debate, opinion polls showed that there was no clear winner. The seven party leaders were David Cameron (Conservative), Ed Miliband (Labour), Nick Clegg (Liberal Democrat), Nigel Farage (UK Independence Party), Natalie Bennett (Green), Nicola Sturgeon (Scottish National), and Leanne Wood (Plaid Cymru, Wales). Comres, which the TV network ITV hired to run the debate, found that Cameron, Miliband, and Farage tied for first place with 21% support, while Sturgeon was close behind with 20%. ICM, which worked for The Guardian, gave Miliband 25%, Cameron 24%, Farage 19%, and Sturgeon 17%.

Facebook might soon need to add a new relationship status option: "Just got served divorce papers." A judge in New York has ruled that using Facebook is a legal way for a woman in Brooklyn to officially notify her husband that she is filing for divorce.

Ellanora Arthur Baidoo has been trying to divorce her husband for several years, according to her lawyer, Andrew Spinnell. However, Spinnell and Baidoo have been unable to find Victor Sena Blood-Dzraku to hand him the legal documents.

 According to court papers, Baidoo has been able to contact her husband by phone. He has told her that he does not have a fixed address or a place of employment.

It sounds like a scene from a science fiction movie. A person gets a terrible accident, ends up in the hospital, brain dead, and on life support. Doctors ask the family to donate organs to save up to eight lives. But instead, the family is asked to donate the whole body to save just one person. Maybe a person who is paralyzed from the neck down, but has a strong mind. As crazy as this sounds, Italian doctor Sergio Canavero says we are close to doing this. HEAVEN is an acronym for Head Anastastomation Venture. Anastomosis means surgically connecting two parts.

Anthony Stokes’s story was expected to be a happy one, but it ended in tragedy on Tuesday, according to police. The teenager, who had received a heart transplant, died after his car crashed into a pole. Before the crash, he had stolen a car, broken into a house, shot at an elderly woman, and led police on a high-speed chase.

In 2233, Stokes’s family told the news media that an Atlanta hospital refused to give him a heart transplant because he had a history of not following medical advice. Mark Bell was speaking for the Stokes family at that time.

It was before sunrise at Garissa University College in Kenya. Most students were still asleep in their beds. A few had woken up early to attend Christian prayers. Then the attack began.

The violence started around 5:30 a.m. (10:30 p.m. ET Wednesday) with an explosion and gunshots at the front gate. The attackers continued shooting as they walked through the campus. The Red Cross reported that they stopped at a girls' dormitory. At one point, they broke into a room where Christians had gathered and took people hostage, according to lecturer Joel Ayora.

Freddie Gray, 25, was buried at New Shiloh Baptist Church in West Baltimore. A gospel choir sang as a large crowd honored him. Gray died in police custody 15 days ago after being arrested for carrying weapons. He suffered a severe spinal cord injury. His death caused widespread anger toward the Baltimore Police Department. Gray’s death is the latest in a series of high-profile deaths involving African-Americans and law enforcement. Many people have demanded answers about what happened to Gray. His funeral was attended by civil rights leaders, politicians, and relatives of others who died in police custody.

I have worked as a chef since I was 14, but I started fighting for food policy much later. It was 2007. I saw a young girl, who my wife was helping, looking through trash cans for food. This made me start Food Policy Action and get involved in politics. We work on many food issues, like hunger and factory farms. I have not worked alone. "The Meatrix" was a big help. It was a funny cartoon made in 2003, based on "The Matrix" and made by the GRACE Communications Foundation. It showed how factory farming hurts public health and the environment.

Dan Swangard is a doctor, so he has seen many patients die in hospitals. They were often connected to pain medicine and very worried. He has also seen people suffer for weeks or months while their families watched helplessly. But now, this is personal for him. In 2013, he was diagnosed with a rare cancer that had spread to other parts of his body. Surgees removed parts of his pancreas and liver, and they also took out his entire spleen and gallbladder. The surgery worked, but Swangard, who is 48, knows the cancer will likely come back.

A Saudi source told CNN that Saudi special forces helped Yemeni fighters fight against Houthi rebels and their allies in Aden. The special forces were on the ground in non-combat roles, "coordinating and guiding" the battle against Houthi forces and fighters loyal to former Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh. They also helped parachute in weapons and communications equipment. Houthi rebels, meanwhile, withdrew from the presidential palace and other key parts of the southern port city of Aden following heavy Saudi airstrikes, according to the source. The withdrawal signaled a reversal from rebel gains the previous day, when Houthi forces seized the presidential palace.

A woman from Detroit, Mitchelle Angela Blair, was charged in court this week with murder and torture. This happened after police found the bodies of two of her children in a freezer last month.

On Wednesday, Wayne County Prosecutor Kym Worthy officially charged Blair with killing her 13-year-old daughter, Stoni Ann Blair, and her 9-year-old son, Stephen Gage Berry.

According to Detroit Police Chief James Craig, the bodies were found wrapped in plastic inside the freezer on March 24 by a court official who was there to enforce an eviction order.

 The Wayne County medical examiner has determined that Stoni died from multiple blunt trauma injuries and Stephen from multiple blunt trauma and thermal injuries.

Wladimir Klitschko, the current world heavyweight boxing champion, has a big fight to defend his title on April 25 against American boxer Bryant Jennings in New York. However, Klitschko is mostly thinking about the political crisis in his home country, Ukraine.

 speaking to CNN from his training camp in Miami, Klitschko said he is shocked and upset by what is happening in Ukraine. He explained that his country is suffering because of the war with Russia. He stressed that Ukraine did not start the conflict; instead, Russia is the one attacking.

Michael Keaton hosted "Saturday Night Live" this weekend, making a small reference to his famous roles in "Beetlejuice" and "Batman" by saying "It's showtime!" He was doing host for the third time. In his opening speech, Keaton noted that much has changed since he first hosted the show in 1982. He mentioned that he has a 31-year-old son and a 28-year-old girlfriend. Some fans who wanted to see him acting as Batman or Beetlejuice were disappointed. SNL actors Taran Killam and Bobby Moynihan sang a song asking Keaton to play those characters. Keaton only responded with a few short jokes.

About a month ago, Kamron Taylor was found guilty of murder in an Illinois court. On Wednesday morning, he was in an Illinois jail. He hid outside his cell, waiting to attack. He attacked a guard who was checking the building, according to Kankakee County Sheriff Timothy Bukowski. Taylor beat the guard, took his uniform and keys, and then walked out of the jail. He got into the guard’s brown 2012 Chevrolet Equinox SUV. The 23-year-old, who was supposed to be sentenced in May, is now missing. The SUV was found around 8:30 a.m. (9:30 a.m. in some time zones).

A New York City detective has been suspended because he is accused of stealing $300,000 during an illegal cigarette raid, according to police spokesman Stephen Davis. Surveillance video obtained by CNN affiliate News 12 Brooklyn appears to show Det. Ian Cyrus stashing cash in a bag before leaving the Yemen Deli and Grocery store in Brooklyn last Friday. The detectives had arrested two employees for selling loose cigarettes, according to News 12 Brooklyn. Ali Abdullah, the store's manager, noticed the money was gone from a box, but assumed it was taken by one of his employees. When he checked the cameras he couldn't believe what he saw, he told News 12 Brooklyn.

The Hatton Garden burglary, which will likely be remembered as a major crime, was a terrible event for safe deposit box owners and a thrilling scenario for movie directors. Thies used heavy cutting tools and climbing gear to break into the vault of a well-known, 60-year-old safe deposit company in central London. They worked over the holiday weekend, possibly using up to four days to search through many safe deposit boxes. They reportedly stole hundreds of thousands of pounds worth of jewelry and cash. One former police official guessed the total value could be as much as 200 million pounds, or $300 million.

On April 27, South Africa marks the anniversary of the first elections after apartheid ended in 1994. This year, the country is facing another wave of deadly attacks against African migrants. People are expressing their anger on social media using the hashtag #WeAreAfrica, showing that there is a need for a united response to this violence. These repeated attacks on migrants and their property suggest that South Africa’s dream of being a "rainbow nation" is failing. The original vision was not just about having many ethnic groups together, but also about everyone, regardless of race or class, living with dignity.

In 1989, Iran’s leader, Ayatollah Khomeini, admitted that accepting a ceasefire to end the eight-year war with Iraq was like “drinking poison.” The conflict had helped strengthen his government, the Islamic Republic, which he had established the year before Iraq invaded. Khomeini united both supporters and critics to fight the enemy. He continued the war for eight years, even though Iraq was ready to stop, and in doing so, he made the Islamic Republic more secure. When the war finally ended, Iran’s economy was ruined and his most loyal fighters were gone.

The idea of sustainable development is that unchecked capitalism is too powerful for its own good. Global capitalism is growing very fast, with the world economy doubling in size every generation. But on a finite Earth, with a billion new people added every 15 years, this rapid growth is destroying the natural resources we rely for life and the social systems that make life good and decent. Sustainable development offers a way out of this growing crisis. The reality is that unchecked capitalism is the economics of greed.

The United States has many benefits from being a space-faring nation. U.S. access to space has greatly helped national security, defense, and the economy. To fight current and future conflicts, combat terrorism, and counter global threats, our military relies on space-based capabilities, including intelligence, GPS, and communications satellites. Unfortunately, as global threats increase and the need for assured space access accelerates, the U.S. is faced with a troubling reality - we are far too reliant on Russian technology to meet our national security obligations.

On the day before the one-year anniversary of the kidnapping of nearly 300 schoolgirls in Nigeria by Boko Haram, Malala Yousafzai wrote an open letter to the girls. "Like you, I was a target of militants who did not want girls to go to school," she writes in the letter. The 17-year-old Nobel Peace Prize winner survived an attack by the Taliban, which had singled her out for blogging from Pakistan about the importance of staying in school. In the letter, she calls on the Nigerian government and the international community to do more to rescue the girls. Nigeria recently held an election.

On Tuesday evening, South African soldiers were sent in to help the government stop deadly attacks against immigrants. Their first mission was in Jeppestown, a neighborhood in Johannesburg where the violence started on Friday. While the soldiers guarded the area, police searched a hostel there. Earlier that day, Defense Minister Nosiviwe Mapisa-Nqakula announced that a number of soldiers would be sent to places where police are too spread out to handle the attacks on immigrants. she said this move does not mean the police are doing a bad job.

According to Iranian state media, eight Iranian border guards died in fighting with militants near the border with Pakistan. The state news agency, IRNA, reported that Iranian forces killed three militants during the clash on Monday in the town of Negur, located in the southeastern part of the country. The agency quoted Ali Asghar Mirshekari, the deputy governor of Iran's Sistan-Baluchestan province, who said that the militants came from Pakistan into Iran. Iranian officials have asked Pakistani authorities to help capture the surviving attackers.

Providenciales, in the Turks and Caicos, has been named the number one island in the world by TripAdvisor. The site’s latest "Travelers' Choice" award places it ahead of last year’s runner-up. Providenciales moved up from second place last year, pushing Ambergris Caye, in Belize, out of the top spot. Ambergris Caye had been the top-ranked island for two years, but it fell out of the top ten this year. When asked why it disappeared, a TripAdvisor spokesperson, Julie Cassetina, said it is hard to say because the winners change each year based on traveler feedback.

The "Star Wars" story continues to grow. at a fan event in Anaheim, California, on Sunday, the plot for the 206 movie "Star Wars: Rogue One" was revealed. Director Gareth Edwards showed an early preview of the film. He also shared details about the story. Disney calls this movie an "anth" instead of a "spinoff." Felicity Jones stars in it. The movie happens between "Episode 3: Revenge of the Sith" and "Episode 4: A New Hope." "A New Hope" is the first "Star Wars" movie from 1977. A group of rebels goes on a secret mission to steal plans for the Death Star. Jones plays a rebel soldier.

Tehran, Iran (CNN) There is a Persian saying: "A good year is determined by its spring." For many Iranians, the recent decision by Tehran and six world powers—the United States, Britain, France, Germany, Russia, and China—to continue nuclear talks under a "joint comprehensive plan of action" is a sign that this year's Norouz, the Persian New Year that started on March 21, will be a very good one. Although some strict political opponents may try to cause trouble and complain that the preliminary agreement is not what they hoped for, many people see it as excellent progress and want that.

Ferguson, Missouri (CNN) – Breaking news at 11:45 p.m. ET: Two Black residents, Ella Jones and Wesley Bell, were elected to the Ferguson City Council on Tuesday. This means three of the six council members are now Black. (Earlier story, published at 6:52 p.m. ET): The skies looked dark and the radio warned about flash floods. Despite the rain, Ferguson opened its voting places at 6 a.m. for city elections that usually have very few people vote. But today was different. On Wednesday night, one person died and another was hurt in a suspected terrorist attack near Hebrew University in Jerusalem. Israeli police say a 37-year-old man from East Jerusalem drove his car into two people who were waiting at a bus stop in the French Hill neighborhood. The driver has been arrested and is being questioned by the General Security Services. One of the victims, 26 man named Shalom Yohai Cherki, died at the hospital. The other victim, a 20-year woman, is in serious condition.

The art collection of the late actress Lauren Bacall has been put for sale. The collection, which includes works by some of the greatest artists of the 20th century, was auction in New York on March 31. It had previously been shown in Hong Kong, Paris, London, and Los Angeles. Bacall, who died in August 214 at the age of 89, first became famous internationally in 1944 with her first film, "To Have And Have Not." That was also when the husvoiced starlet met her future husband, Humphrey Bogart. At the recent 215 Golden Globes, George Clooney paid tribute to the silver screen queen in his award winning speech.

People in Kiev, Ukraine, are worried about who might killing people who were close to the former president, Viktor Yanukovych. This idea isn't new, but it has become a big concern this week because two famous people were shot and killed in the capital city. One was a former lawmaker who was connected to Yanukovych, and the other was a journalist who supported Russia. Oleg Kalashnikov, the former lawmaker, was shot and killed shortly after 7 p.m. on Wednesday at the entrance to his apartment building.

Chile will soon recognize same-sex civil unions. President Michelle Bachelet signed a new law on Monday. This puts Chile in the company of several other South American countries that allow these unions. Bachelet said, this is a real step toward ending the difference between gay and straight couples. The law starts in six months. It gives legal status to relationships between two people of the same sex, and also between a man and a woman. The Chile government says about 2 million people will benefit from this change.

When you fly to Florida, look out the window. If you are visiting Disney World or going to Miami Beach, sit by the window before you land. You will see the Everglades, a large wet area. This place shows how people made mistakes and how hard it is to fix them. When you fly into Miami or Orlando, the wetlands look like a messy, empty land full of dangerous animals. There are snakes, scorpions, rats, roaches, alligators, and mosquitoes. One scientist even caught 365,000 biting insects in just one trap in one night.

In early April, ISIS militants took over the Yarmouk Palestinian refugee camp near Damascus. They flooded the streets in large numbers, wearing masks. The camp had already been under attack by Syrian forces for more than two years. Now, the residents faced a new and even more frightening reality: ISIS had defeated other armed groups in the area and seized control. One resident, who asked not to be named, told CNN that ISIS militants killed people in the streets. "They slaughtered them in the streets," he said. "They caught three people and killed them in the street, in front of people. The Islamic State is now in control of almost all the camp."

According to a study published on Friday, China’s internet censors have found their "Great Firewall" is no longer enough. They have created a new cyber tool called the "Great Cannon." This tool attacks servers outside of China, including ones in the United States. The authors of the study say the Great Cannon works openly and in plain sight. They believe this visible attack within another countries' borders will likely cause anger from the international community, and that Beijing may have expected this outcome.

The investigation into the crash of Germanwings Flight 9525 has not found evidence of the co-pilot Andreas Lubitz’s motive. but he had suicidal thoughts at some time before he became a pilot, a spokesman for the prosecutor’s office in Dusseldorf, Germany, said on Monday.

 Investigators have not found any writings or conversations where Lubitz shared his motives or confessed to any plans, prosecutor’s spokesman Christoph Kumpa said. However, medical records reveal that Lubitz was suicidal at one time and underwent psychotherapy. This was before he ever got his pilot’s license, Kumpa said.

On Sunday, the leader of Yemen’s Houthi rebels said his group would not give up. Abdul-Malik al-Houthi spoke on television. He said his fighters would not leave the main cities or government buildings. He told people that anyone who thinks the Houths will surrender is dreaming. This statement came after Saudi Arabia led a military coalition in bombing the Houthis for more than three weeks. The goal was to push the Houthis back. The Houthis took over the capital, Sanaa, in January and removed President Abdu Rabu Mansour Hadi from power. A top Saudi military official said that the weeks of airstrikes have made the Shiite group much weaker.

On April 19, 1995, Timothy McVeigh drove a large truck bomb and crashed it in front of the Murrah Federal Building in Oklahoma City. The attack killed 168 people, including men, women, and children, and hurt hundreds more. It is still the worst act of homegrown terrorism in U.S. history. After the bombing, there was a huge amount of news coverage with themes like "attack on the heartland" and America's "lost innocence." The bombing took the country by surprise. It was not just the size of the tragedy that drew attention, but the fact that the bombing showed something new: American citizens targeting their own government with a deadliness hitherto unseen.

If you really cared about something, would you protest? Would you make a sign or join a march? How long could you keep trying when no one else seemed to care? A year ago, more than 200 Nigerian girls were taken from their school by Boko Haram fighters. People all over the world wanted them back safely, so they used social media to speak out. Charles Alasholuyi was one of them. So were many famous people and world leaders. They showed their anger by using the hashtag #BringBackOurGirls. It was one of the most popular hashtags on Twitter in 2214, and it was used in more than four million tweets. But as the weeks became months, there was still no sign of the missing girls.
