Barney Frank, a retired U.S. Congressman, recently spoke in Chicago. He told a full audience about his 45 years of public service. Frank was the first member of Congress to marry someone of the same sex while in office. He also criticized politicians who hide their sexual identity but vote against gay rights. When an audience member asked about a California ballot measure that would allow killing gay people, Frank said he did not know about it.

Al-Shabaab militants attacked Garissa University College in Kenya on Thursday morning. during morning prayers. The gunmen shot people randomly and took some students hostage. Security forces killed the attackers. Nearly 150 people died, including students, and dozens more were hurt. The U.S. Embassy in Nairobi said Al-Shabaab claimed responsibility. This attack happened only months after Al-Shabaab killed non-Muslim workers in a Kenyan quarry. The terrorist group has been responsible for many attacks in the area. They have also recruited some Americans, especially from the Somali-American community in Minnesota.

A university in South Africa has removed a statue of Cecil Rhodes, a British colonial leader, after several weeks of protests. Students at the University of Cape Town used social media to demand the statue be removed, arguing that his history is connected with racism. They started a campaign last month using the hashtag #RhodesMustFall. Now, four weeks later, the hashtag is #RhodesHasFallen. On Wednesday, the university announced that a heritage authority gave permission for the statue to be taken down from the campus. The university stated in a press release that these actions are being taken to keep the statue safe while decisions about its future are being made.

Syria is becoming a terrible place, and the situation is getting worse. According to an opposition group, the number of people who have died has doubled in just one year. The Syrian Observatory for Human Rights reported on Thursday that 310,00 people have been killed since the civil war started. A year before that, the number was 162,402. The year before that, the United Nations said 70,000 people had died. The United Nations says that more than half of Syrians are so poor that they desperately need help to survive. Food rations are being reduced because there is not enough money donated.

Ailina Tsarnaeva went into Manhattan Criminal Court quietly, looking almost shy. But prosecutors say she was not shy when dealing with someone she saw as a rival.

According to a criminal complaint, Tsarnaeva threatened a woman in a phone call this summer. She said, "Leave my man alone." She also said, "Stop looking for him. I know people who can put a bomb where you live."

Because prosecutors knew who was making the threats, they did not think it was a joke. They charged Tsarnaeva with aggravated harassment. Tsarnaeva denies this charge.

Last December, when she left court, she and her lawyer refused to talk about the case. Tsarnaeva is the sister of Dzhokhar and Tamerlan Tsarnaev.

A police officer in Gaza told CNN that police took a door with a drawing by British artist Banksy on Thursday. The seizure happened after a disagreement about selling the door. The door’s owner, Rabea Darduna, filed a complaint with a Gaza court. He said he did not know how much the door was worth when he sold it for just $175. The iron door will stay with the Khan Younis police in southern Gaza until a court hearing. The date for the hearing has not been set yet. Darduna says that when his home in Gaza was destroyed in last summer’s war, he felt he had nothing left. Only a doorway and a door.

The Saudi-led coalition’s attacks on Houthi rebels in Yemen continued on Tuesday. The coalition is gaining more control, while many locals are fleeing the violence and death toll rises, including dozens of civilians. Five days after the first airstrikes, the coalition has destroyed the Houthis’ air defense systems and the systems of supporters of former President Ali Abdullah Saleh. made almost all air bases and runways unusable, a Saudi source said. Saudi Arabia’s navy now controls all Yemeni ports, allowing only carefully monitored non-military medical goods to pass through its blockade, according to the source.

Guus Hiddink, the manager of the Netherlands team, strongly criticized his own fans for booing Spanish player Andres Iniesta during the Netherlands' 2-0 win against Spain on Tuesday. He called the fans a "disgrace."



Spain's coach, Vicente del Bosque, used a new lineup for the game in Amsterdam. Iniesta, who started on the bench, came into the game in the 76th minute. The home fans cheered and booed him.

The Netherlands won thanks to goals from defender Stefan de Vrij and midfielder Davy Klaassen in the first half. This was a good win for the team's confidence. However, Hiddink was unhappy with how Iniesta was treated.

On May 21, Scotland will learn if its Euro 2016 soccer match against Georgia in September will be played without fans. UEFA has started disciplinary action against the Georgian Football Federation. This happened because fans entered the field twice during Georgia’s 2-0 loss to Germany in Tbilisi on Sunday. UEFA also will investigate other charges, including home fans setting off fireworks. There are also safety breaches, including blocked stairs, locked gates, and no body searches by staff at the Boris Paichadze Stadium. A fan enters the field during Georgia’s 2-0 loss to Germany on Sunday in Tbilisi.

On Wednesday, football agents were waiting to hear about new rules. starting April 1, the rules for becoming a football agent will change. Now, anyone can become an agent if they pay £500 for the first year. After that, the Football Association (FA) will charge £250 each year to renew the license. This does not apply to agents who already have a license. The FA was supposed to put a link on their website so agents could sign up, but by 1pm the link was not there yet. Mel Stein believes the new rules will cause chaos. These new guidelines came after FIFA stopped controlling the agent business.

Maksims Uvarenko, the Latvian goalkeeper for CSKA Sofia, hasn’t been paid in three months. He has asked his parents to send money to pay his rent. Even though he has money problems, Uvarenko likes the fans. He says they are unique and very supportive. Uvarenko joined the Bulgarian club in January for 18 months. He told local media on Wednesday, “The lack of money is the biggest problem I've faced at CSKA. I still haven't received any salary and I've been at the club for three months.”

David Moore, 25, was angry and lost his control on the road. He had just left his house and was stuck in heavy traffic next to Rafal Cegielka, 45. Rafal was driving his child to St John's Primary School in Burnley, Lancashire.

A court heard that David hit Rafal in the face. Then, David broke Rafal's car with a hockey stick. This happened in front of young children. David said he was having a bad day and got very angry.

Spain lost 2-0 to Holland on Tuesday. This sad result reminds people of Spain’s bad performance at the 2014 World Cup. Gerard Pique, a Spanish player, says coach Vicente del Bosque should not be too worried about losing three friend games in a row. Holland scored two early goals. They kept Spain from scoring in the second half. This win for Holland was at the Amsterdam Arena. It was similar to when Holland beat Spain 5-1 in the 2014 World Cup in Brazil. That game ended Spain’s six years of being the best team in the world.

Police say a New York City mother, Ulrike Berger, 44, has taken her seven-year-old daughter, Kaia, to Germany during a custody dispute. A court order forb Berger from leaving the United States with the child. On March 22, one day after Kaia was dropped off for a weekend visit, the mother and daughter are believed to have flown to Europe. Police are searching for them. They believe the pair left New York for Germany on March 22, breaking the custody court order. Police say the last place they were seen was Berger’s home in Boerun Hill, Brooklyn, at 10 a.m. on March 21, when Kaia’s father dropped her off.

A large fire burned through dry heathland near the south coast of Britain. The flames were high, and thick, black smoke rose into the sky. The fire destroyed an area the size of 100 football pitches. This happened after days of storms that knocked down trees and closed roads. The 70-hehectare area in Dorset was very dry because it is on a hillside and water runs off the slope. Fire investigators say the fire was started on purpose. Three separate areas of heheland were destroyed: one was half a hectare, another was one hectare, and the largest was 70 hectares.

Last night, emergency services in Britain received 600 calls per hour during New Year 2012 celebrations. Paramedics were overwhelmed, and in Cambridge, a Territorial Army field hospital was set up to treat drunk partygoers. The London Ambulance Service reported that at its peak, they were handling over 600 calls per hour, which is more than three times as many as on a normal night. In Manchester, a man collapsed on the pavement next to an ambulance while two partygoers walked past eating a late-night takeaway. In another scene in Manchester, a man was slumped over in a doorway as two women walked by celebrating the New Year.

Liverpool goalkeeper Simon Mignolet says that his strong mind helped him get over being dropped from the team last December. Manager Brendan Rodgers took Mignolet out of the team "for an unknown time" because of his bad play. But Mignolet came back quickly when another player, Brad Jones, hurt his thigh. The 27-year-old from Belgium said he tried to stay happy even though he was upset about being removed. Simon Mignolet showed how his strong mind helped him recover after being dropped. Mignolet (second right) made a save from a free kick during a league game against Swansea last month. Mignolet told FourFourTwo: "I was positive."

On Tuesday, large hailstones, as big as plums, fell in the Southern United States. The unusual weather made people run outside to take videos. Arke USA from Bryant, Arkansas, filmed ice balls hitting his backyard and spling into his swimming pool. The video shows the hailstones falling fast and many breaking when they hit the ground. Even though it was about 80 degrees, the hard ice did not melt quickly. In just a few seconds, the patio was covered in white ice.

The crew of a replica pirate ship, the Liana's Ransom, was forced to leave their boat because it lost power in rough seas off the coast of Maine.

The Coast Guard rescued nine crew members with lifeboats on Tuesday. The Canadian charter ship was left drifting 30 miles east of Portland.

The ship reported engine problems around 12:35 a.m. on Monday. and said the sails were tangled around the mast.

Amazing photos show blue glowing algae along Australia's east coast. The pictures were taken in Jervis Bay on the south coast of New South Wales. The bright blue light made up one of Australia's popular beaches. Photographer Andy Hutchinson said the scene was beautiful and looked supernatural. It was caused by millions of tiny plankton giving off light. A similar event happened at Sydney's Manly Beach in August 21, 214. An ocean expert told Daily Mail Australia that people should not worry about the algae.

17 Rahul Kumar, a drunk teenager, was rescued by security guards after he jumped into a lion enclosure at a zoo in western India. The incident happened at the Kamla Nehru Zoological Park in Ahmedabad.

Kumar climbed over the fence and ran toward the lions, shouting that he would "kill them." He later explained that he was drunk and thought he had a good chance against the animals.

Kumar had been sitting near the enclosure when he suddenly ran toward the lions, surprising the zoo security. He shouted, "Today I kill a lion!"

A 12-year-old boy in Nanchang, China, survived after falling out of a fifth-story window onto a car parked below. The incident occurred last Saturday. According to his father, the boy likely fell while sleepwalking. A hotel receptionist across the street heard a loud bang around midnight, which she thought was a car accident. The People’s Daily Online reported the story.

Drew Miller, a player for the Detroit Red Wings, said he is excited to play again. He got a serious cut on his face just yesterday that could have made him blind. Miller said, "I feel very lucky that the skate did not hit my eye."

During practice on Wednesday, Miller wore a full face mask. He had a large, bloody wound that needed 50 or 60 stitches to close. The stitches went through several layers of skin. The Detroit Free Press reported this. Miller now has a scar across his eye. However, he did not lose his eyesight after another player cut his face with a skate.

Filipe Luis says he wants to stay at Chelsea until his contract ends next year, even though Atletico Madrid might try to sign him again this summer. The full-back signed a three-year deal when he moved from Atletico last July, but he has had trouble making the left-back position his own at Chelsea. Atletico might hope this gives them an advantage, but Luis said, “I am happy at Chelsea. I want to stay at the club until the end of my contract.”

22-year-old Charlie Sumner, a fan of Reading Football Club, is facing a three-year ban from football. He ran onto the playing field topless and did four front flips during his first game at the Madejski Stadium. This happened during an FA Cup match last month, where Reading beat Bradford City 3-0. Sumner, who said going to his first game was a "brillt experience," was tackled by security staff after landing on his back.

A video shows a van carrying about six men on its roof swerving and then tipping over. The incident happened on a road near Salé, Morocco. The van was likely carrying football fans. A car following the van recorded the footage. The video shows the van moving side to side on a busy road before it falls onto its side.

England’s Under-17 soccer team plays in Group D of the UEFA Under-17 European Championships. The tournament is held in Bulgaria in May. England’s opponents are the Republic of Ireland, Holland, and Italy.

 England is the current European champion. They won last year’s final in Malta by beating Holland on penalties. To move on to the quarter-finals, England must beat Holland again. This year’s tournament is bigger than before. It now has 16 teams instead of eight. This is the first time the tournament has been expanded.

 John Peacock is the coach of England’s team. Danny Collinge scored England’s first goal against Norway during the qualifying matches.

An elephant was relaxing by a small pool in South Africa’s Kruger National Park with its family. A male buffalo came too close, which made the elephant angry. The elephant tried to spray water from its trunk at the buffalo to make it leave, but missed. The video shows the frustrated elephant trying again. The baby elephant stayed close to its parent for protection while the buffalo drank from the pool.

Michael Thorpe, a former pub owner, won an eight-year legal battle to overturn his conviction for illegally showing foreign TV channels that broadcast Premier League football matches. Thorpe, 55, was convicted in November 2006 for showing a Premier League game at the Stoke Inn in Plymouth, Devon, without an agreement with the official broadcasters. Thorpe says he paid a heavy price for the lengthy fight to get his conviction quashed and has lost his pub as a result.

The Irish Football Association (IFA) is worried about structural damage at Windsor Park, their stadium in Belfast. They hope this won't stop the team from playing a very important Euro 2016 match against Romania in June.

On Tuesday morning, cracks were found in the West Stand. The area was closed off while engineers checked the damage. A spokesperson said the IFA found out about the damage that happened overnight on Monday night.

22-year-old Charlie Sumner, a football fan, is facing a three-year ban. He ran onto the field topless and did several somersaults during his first game at the stadium. Sumner invaded the pitch alone at Reading's Madejski Stadium during an FA Cup quarter final replay against Bradford City last month. The Reading supporter, whose team was leading 3-0 at the time, did four front flips on the field, landing on his back each time, before being stopped by security staff.

A BMW driver was arrested today after a student was hit and killed while walking to the library. The driver had five children in the car. Hina Shamim, 21, died near the University of Kingston in London last night, just weeks before her 22nd birthday. Friends left flowers at the scene today. They said Miss Shamim, who was from Peterborough and had the nickname "Hyena," was very much loved and was "the most charming lovely girl in the world."

A mother and her teenage daughter were arrested because a video of them fighting with a student at Langham Creek High School in Houston was posted online. The incident happened on Tuesday. The mother, who has not been named, was reportedly angry because her daughter said the other girl had been bullying her. The video shows the mother, wearing a black top, on the right, and the victim, wearing white, in the center.

Stoke City’s chief executive, Tony Scholes, hopes they can keep Asmir Begovic. The goalkeeper is in the final year of his contract. Begovic, who plays for Bosnia, has often been linked with other teams while playing at the Britannia Stadium. His contract has just over 12 months left. Scholes thinks they can match the 27-year-old’s goals. “Asmir is clearly a great goalkeeper and we really want to keep him at the club,” he told The Sentinel. “When you have very good players, it is only natural that there will be rumors about their future.”

A bus driver in Auckland, New Zealand, was fired by his boss for reading a newspaper while driving. The bus company, Ritchies Coachlines, called the driver a "complete idiot."

A passenger recorded the driver flipping through the newspaper pages while the bus was moving and sent the video to the company with a complaint. The video shows the driver looking at a page when the bus stops at a traffic light. The boss, Andrew Ritchie, said he was embarrassed by the driver's actions.

West Ham manager Sam Allardyce says defender Winston Reid will play on Saturday against Leicester City. However, Enner Valencia will not be available. Reid has not played since March 4, when he hurt his hamstring in a 1-0 loss to Chelsea. He returned to full training during the break. Valencia missed the last two games against Arsenal and Sunderland because of a toe injury from mid-March. Allardyce says Valencia is not ready to play yet.

Five days before his wedding last May, Brittany Huber and John Redman were in a terrible car crash on a highway in Georgia. Brittany died, and John was badly hurt. John survived, but his body was severely damaged. Doctors said he would probably spend the rest of his life in a nursing home and use a wheelchair. The 25-year-old, who was an assistant basketball coach at Dalton State College, had a very difficult future ahead of him. However, against all expectations, John recovered. On March 24, he helped his team win a championship title.

Lucas, playing on the left, was seen with Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard at a charity match at Anfield on Sunday. Lucas, a midfielder for Liverpool, wants to return to his best form after recovering from an injury. From late November until February, he started 16 games out of 19, and the team’s results improved during this time. However, a groin injury in the Merseyside derby in February kept him out for 10 games. He was an unused substitute in the loss to Manchester United, which was the team’s first league defeat since mid-December. but he played the full 90 minutes in Sunday’s All-Star Charity game at Anfield.

Are you tired of boring father-daughter photos? Japanese photographer Yûki Aoyama has found a fun way to make them more interesting. In her new book, titled "Daughter and Salary Man," she shows serious-looking teenage daughters standing next to their fathers who are jumping in the air. The daughters look at the camera and smile, while their fathers strike dramatic poses.

Police are looking for a man, who is between 50 and 60 years old, for robbing a bank. He took £3,000 in cash and ran away. The robbery happened at 12:30 pm at a Lloyds Bank in Fairwater, Cardiff.

Police have released pictures from security cameras showing the suspect. He is a white man with greying black hair and glasses. He is between 5ft 9in and 6ft tall and was wearing black clothes. The video shows him inside the bank.

No one was hurt during the robbery. Police are sure that members of the public can identify him.

The Court of Arbitration for Sport has ended Morocco's ban from the next two African Cup of Nations. This was originally decided by the Confederation of African Football (CAF). Morocco was kicked out of the 2017 and 2019 tournaments and was fined $1 million. CAF also wanted $9 million more in compensation because Morocco quit as the host country due to fear of the Ebola disease. The Ivory Coast won the tournament that was held in Equatorial Guinea. Morocco can now take part in the next two African Cup of Nations.

Tom Boyd thinks that Jason Denayer’s time on loan at Celtic has been so successful that he is now ready to compete for a spot at Manchester City next season. This would mean Ronny Deila’s plan to keep the young Belgian player for another year would fail, but Boyd also sees a good side of it. According to the former Celtic captain, Denayer’s growth can serve as a perfect advertisement to encourage more young talents to take their next career step at Parkhead. Young defender Jason Denayer (left) has impressed on loan at Celtic this season. The 19-year-old recently won his first international cap for Belgium in a Euro 2016 qualifier against Cyprus.

Andros Townsend scored a amazing goal for England in Italy, and he said that critics like Paul Merson gave him the motivation he needed. This has been a confusing season for the 23-year-old, who has not played as well as he did when he first started playing for the national team. England’s manager, Roy Hodgson, has still trusted him, and Townsend showed his thanks with an excellent goal at Juventus Stadium. Andros Townsend scored England’s equal goal in their 1-1 friendly match against Italy in Turin on Tuesday night. Townsend celebrates his goal with his Tottenham teammates, Ryan Mason (left) and Kyle Walker.

Chinese company Dalian Wanda Group has officially bought 20% of Spanish football team Atletico Madrid. The deal was approved at a special meeting on Tuesday. Wanda’s legal team signed papers to buy 726,707 shares for €45 million (£32.8 million). The deal was first announced in January, but two special meetings were needed to make the deal official. Wanda’s chairman, Wang Jianlin, wants to make Atletico Madrid more famous in Asia. Atletico Madrid’s manager, Diego Simeone, talks to the media.

Antonio Conte said that his return to Turin for Italy’s 1-1 draw against England brought back “very fond memories,” despite reports that he received death threats in the days before the friendly match. Conte, who was the former manager of Juventus, took over as Italy’s head coach in August, replacing Cesare Prandelli after the team was eliminated in the group stage of the World Cup last summer. However, his first seven months as the national team’s manager have been very difficult. Italy needed a late goal from Eder to save a 2-2 tie against Bulgaria last Saturday, and Conte reportedly received death threats from Juventus fans after Claudio Marchisio suffered a knee injury on the day before the Euro 216 qualifier.

Ian Murray thinks that the final month of the Scottish Championship season could be easier for Hibernian, allowing them to overtake Rangers for second place. His team, Dumbarton, has already played both of his former clubs this season and will face them again in the coming weeks.

Murray does not believe that Rangers will be able to keep up their current speed. Even though Rangers are currently winning games, he expects the advantage to shift back to Hibernian soon.

Simon Mignolet, the goalkeeper for Liverpool, posted photos of himself sitting in an airplane cockpit with the pilots. He was flying back to England after playing for the Belgian national team in Euro 2016 qualifiers against Cyprus and Israel. Mignolet was on the list of players for both games, but he was not allowed to play because the team chose another goalkeeper, Thibaut Courtois, from Chelsea. Mignolet has played 14 games for Belgium. He shared the photos on his Facebook page on Wednesday.

Chyknell Hall Estate, a large country property near Bridgnorth in Shropshire, is for sale for £6 million. The property sits on 200 acres of land and includes a Grade II-listed manor house and five cottages. The estate also has a swimming pool, a tennis court, stables, and its own cricket pitch. The main house, Chyknell Hall, was built in 1814 and has 11 bedrooms. It has only been sold twice since it was built. The privacy of the secluded grounds may attract famous buyers.

Two college police officers in Dallas are on administrative leave after a video showed them harassing four students and arresting one of them. The video shows the officers hitting the student before arresting him. The incident happened at El Centro College last Wednesday. Student Charles Adams recorded the video on his phone. He was smoking a cigarette when he saw the officers approach the students, who were waiting for a bus outside the downtown Dallas campus.

Kilmarnock has made Gary Locke the permanent manager. He signed a three-year contract. Locke, 39, used to manage Hearts. Last summer, he joined Kilmarnock as assistant manager under Allan Johnston. In early February, Johnston left, so Locke took charge of the team. Since then, his team has played seven games and lost only once. Locke will speak to the press on Friday morning.

This weekend, one of the biggest events in German football happens. The usual excitement for this match, called "Der Klassiker," has been reduced a bit. Borussia Dortmund and Bayern Munich have won the last five league titles, and Bayern is likely to win again this season. However, these two teams are now far apart in the standings. Bayern has 31 more points than Dortmund, and they are nine places apart. Even with this gap, the game is still very important for both clubs. Jurgen Klopp, the manager of Borussia Dortmund, is seen celebrating with his players after they beat Hannover.

14-year schoolgirl Deva Joseph was stuck at London Stansted airport when easyJet refused to let her on her flight to Spain. because she had two carry-on bags. Deva cried when she was told she couldn't fly home. She offered to pay extra to put the second bag in the cargo hold, but staff said she had to pay by credit card. Deva is too young to have a credit card.

Gordon Robson, 26, killed John Potts, 45, with one punch. Robson was drunk after his grandfather’s funeral. He hit Mr. Potts in the back of the head outside a sports bar. The hit was so hard that it made a loud crack. Mr. Potts fell down and died. Robson has a history of violent crimes. He was sentenced to three and a half year in jail. The attack happened in November last year outside the NE38 Sports Bar in Washington, Tyne and Wear.

Scoring a goal against your old team and taking a perfect free kick are two of the best feelings in football. Ellen White, a star player for Notts County, experienced both of these on Thursday night. She played against Arsenal in the Women's Super League.

In the 26th minute, Notts County was given a free kick near the penalty area. Laura Bassett and Alex Greenwood seemed to confuse each other, with Bassett almost colliding with Greenwood. This caused confusion. Ellen White spun around near the the box and kicked the ball into the corner of the net, scoring against her former club.

High school girls in China are practicing military-style knife drills. 68 girls, aged 16 to 18, from Huizhou Integrated High School’s 27th class, are learning eight high-intensity movements. They shout “kill, stab, slash, and jab” as they perform each move. They are being trained by Inspector Tan, a former special soldier. The knives are not real, according to school official Huang Anruo, who said the daggers are fake.

We spend about one-third of our lives sleeping. Most people don’t think about what their mind and body need during sleep to feel rested every day. The Sleep Health Foundation did a study and found that 30 percent of Australians say they don’t get enough sleep every day. Professor David Hillman says that if you miss sleep, you have to make up for it later to stay healthy all week. Another study also showed that 30 percent of Australians complain about not getting enough sleep each day. Most adults need about eight hours of sleep each night, anywhere from seven to nine hours.

A video shows a fight between neighbors in Perth, Australia. It ends with someone getting hurt by a crowbar. The video was posted on Facebook today. It shows an angry woman shouting racist insults at a group of men who appear to be African. She is standing over her fence. The woman then goes into her neighbor’s front yard. She holds a metal crowbar. She yells at the men and swings the crowbar at them. The men pick up their own weapons. A fight starts. The woman yells, “ “I don’t deal with monkeys. Go on now you f*****g monkeys.”

Valencia’s 19-year-old left back, Jose Luis Gaya, is attracting interest from Manchester City, Arsenal, and Chelsea. These English clubs hope to sign him away from Real Madrid this summer. Sportsmail’s Pete Jenson examines the Spanish under-21 defender. Why are English clubs interested? His release clause is currently £13.5m. Considering that Luke Shaw, who is similar in age and potential, cost £27m, it would be foolish not to be interested; although there would be reservations about his suitability to the Premier League. Jose Luis Gaya (right) in action for Valencia during a La Liga match with Sevilla earlier this season.

Police in Oregon are asking the public for help to find a motorcyclist who saved two teenagers. The incident happened in Salem. A 59 man named Edward West allegedly pulled a gun on the teens and told them, "get ready to die." A stranger on a green motorcycle then rode up and hit the gun out of West's hands with his helmet. This allowed the teens to run away. The police want to find the motorcyclist who helped them.

Tim Sherwood, the manager of Aston Villa, wants his team captain, Ron Vlaar, to show everyone he is back to his best form. Vlaar is ready to play again after recovering from an injury. Sherwood hopes the defender will help the struggling team finish the season strongly. He also warned Vlaar that people might have forgotten how well he played for the Netherlands in the World Cup last year, even though he missed a penalty in the semi-finals. That performance had led to rumors that Manchester United might want to sign him. Now, the club captain is returning to help Aston Villa fight against being relegated from the league. He will play in their match at Old Trafford on Saturday.

Aston Villa manager Tim Sherwood says he is not worried about the club being sold to a new owner this summer. He wants to build the team his way next season, if they stay in the league. The current owner, Randy Lerner, is talking with a potential buyer. People might wonder if Sherwood will keep his job if a new owner takes over. But Sherwood is focused on keeping the team in the league first, and then using the summer break to make long-term plans.

Celtic wants to loan Jason Denayer from Manchester City again next season. But City says no. Manager Manuel Pellegrini says his young players are not ready for the first team. So, players like Denayer will have to come back from their loans to help the team.

Southampton manager Ronald Koeman is waiting to know exactly when Fraser Forster will return from his knee injury before deciding if the team needs to sign another goalkeeper in the summer. Forster had surgery after twisting his knee during a 2-0 win against Burnley two weeks ago. Doctors say he could be back in as little as four months or as long as 12 months. Koeman does not want to give a exact date, because he thinks Kelvin Davis is a good backup. But he admits that if Forster takes longer to heal, the team might have to find another goalkeeper.

Steve Evans, the manager of Rotherham, was angry on the sidelines because his team, which is close to being relegated, lost a narrow game to Birmingham in the Sky Bet Championship. The main reason for his anger was that his team was not given a penalty.

 Birmingham took the lead in the first half with goals from Robert Tesche and Clayton Donaldson. Matt Derbyshire then scored a goal for Rotherham, who were in fourth place near the bottom of the table.

 Rob Kiernan, playing for Birmingham, handled the ball clumsily near the penalty area around the hour mark. This caused Matt Derbyshire, a former Manchester City player, to fall inside the box. However, the referee, Dean Whitestone, did not award a penalty despite Rotherham’s requests

Virgil van Dijk, a defender for Celtic, is worried about his chances of playing for the Netherlands national team. The Dutch team has already let in more goals in five Euro 2016 qualifying matches than they did in their entire World Cup qualifying campaign last time. Guus Hiddink, the coach, has not contacted him. Van Dijk was selected for two squads last year, but after that, he was left out again. When the Dutch team was tied 1-1 with Turkey recently, he was relaxing in the Arabian Gulf with his teammates. Van Dijk has been playing well for Celtic, but he hasn't been chosen to play for the Netherlands national team.

Celtic has complained to the SFA about ticket prices for their Scottish Cup semi-final against Inverness later this month at Hampden. The game's governing body has already come under fire from Caley Thistle fans for scheduling the match for 12.15pm on Sunday, April 18 - before the first trains from Inverness arrive in Glasgow. Now the Parkhead club have made their feeling known after ticket prices were set at £23 for the North and South stands, with the East Stand being £15 for adults and £5 for concessions. Celtic has complained to the SFA over ticket prices for their Scottish Cup semi-final at Hampden this month.

Paul Murray, the interim chairman of Rangers, said on Thursday that the previous management team is entirely responsible for the club being removed from the stock exchange. The club will be forced to leave the Alternative Investment Market (AIM) because it could not find a new advisor to meet the required rules. Murray says the new board’s future plans will not be affected and that planned investments will still happen.

Wayne Rooney and his England teammates were unhappy with how the team started their match in Italy on Tuesday night. The game was sloppy and lacked energy. The Three Lions faced Italy again, nine months after meeting at the World Cup, in a high-profile friendly at Juventus Stadium. England had won seven games in a row, so expectations were high. However, Roy Hodgson’s team struggled in the first half and deservedly fell behind when Graziano Pelle scored with a header in Turin. England captain Wayne Rooney gave instructions during the 1-1 draw against Italy on Tuesday night. Rooney said he and the rest of the England players were upset by their first half performance.

Dundee United’s board responded to strong criticism from two major supporters' groups, Arabtrust and the Federation of Dundee United Supporters Clubs. The groups said they were shocked to learn that 25 percent of the £6.3 million paid in transfer fees for players Ryan Gauld, Andrew Robertson, Stuart Armstrong, and Gary Mackay-Steven went as commissions to unnamed people. The supporters also argued with chairman Stephen Thompson about how much money he has put into the club. The Dundee United board defended themselves by pointing to the team's success on the field.

Kilmarnock will make an official announcement on Friday morning that Gary Locke is their new permanent manager. He will sign a three-year contract. Locke was first asked to manage the team until the end of the season eight weeks ago, after taking over from Allan Johnston in February. The 39-year-old, who previously managed Hearts, thanked the players for their hard work. Their efforts helped him win the support of the new chairman, Jim Mann. Locke will be officially confirmed as the club's new manager on Friday.

Chinese parents are very eager to raise child prodigies, such 10-year-olds who enter university or 4-year-olds who can dance like Michael Jackson. A new basketball star is now emerging. A viral video in China shows a young boy performing amazing basketball skills that would embarrass many professional players. The five-year-old boy, named Mai Zizhuo, has been playing basketball since he was two and half, according to People's Daily Online. The video begins with the small player making a series of baskets, then running around while dribing two basketballs.

Bayern Munich will not have David Alaba for the last games of the season. because he hurt his knee. and he will be out for about seven weeks. Alaba has a torn knee lig. He was out for three months earlier this year with a different knee injury. He got hurt while playing for Austria in a 1-1 tie against Bosnia on Tuesday. The 22-year-old Alaba said, "I am very sad. But I have a big goal and that is to be there at the season finale." David Alaba was tackled by Emir Spahic during Austria's 1-1 draw against Bosnia-Herzegovina.

Hull KR has signed experienced Australian player Dane Tilse from the Canberra Raiders to fill the spots left by Michael Weyman and Ryan Bailey, who both left the team. Tilse, 30, is very tall (6ft 7in) and weighs over 17 stone. He has signed a 2.5-year deal with Hull KR. He will join the team as soon as he finishes the required paperwork, after the Raiders agreed to let him go. Tilse has played 200 games in Australia. He will work with his old teammate from Canberra, Terry Campese, who is now the captain of Hull KR and recently signed a 2-year contract extension. Tilse is a direct replacement for Weyman, who retired last month because of an injury

Mark Burchill, the manager of Livingston football team, thinks that midfielder Darren Cole will still want to play in Sunday’s Petrofac Cup final. Even though the game is only a week after the sad death of his cousin in America. The former Rangers youth player has been grieving over the loss of Shaun Cole, 22, who was found dead on a street in Miami last weekend and is believed to have been hit by a driver who fled the scene. A soldier who had served in Afghanistan, he was on vacation in Florida while on leave and had attended a music festival there before being found on a sidewalk with a head injury that turned out to be fatal. Livingston manager Mark Burchill is hopeful that midfielder Darren Cole will play for his team on Sunday.

Alan Smith strongly denies that Liverpool fans attacked the ambulance he was in after he was seriously injured. This happened nine years ago, when Manchester United lost 1-0 to Liverpool in the FA Cup.

Smith broke his leg and dislocated his ankle in February 26, 26, when he tried to stop a free kick taken by John Arne Riise. At the time, there were reports that Liverpool fans tried to stop Smith from getting to the hospital. They allegedly threw bottles, beer glasses, and stones at the ambulance and even tried to rock the vehicle.

Ronny Deila, the manager of Celtic, confirmed that the club is interested in signing Danny Wilson, the captain of Hearts. Wilson is also a former player for Rangers and Liverpool. Celtic might offer £400,000 for him. Wilson’s contract with Hearts expires in 12 months. Hearts’ owner, Ann Budge, says the club does not need to sell him.

Ronny Deila, the manager of Celtic, says the team will not risk their chances in the Champions League by playing many games during the pre-season. He blames last summer’s tour of the United States, Austria, and Germany for a bad 4-1 loss to Legia Warsaw. The team gets a lot of money for playing these games. They have also played in Australia and Asia in recent years. Ronny Deila and Nir Bitton left the field after losing to Legia Warsaw. They have not yet decided if they will go to America this July.

Franck Ribery says that rumors about Kevin de Bruyne joining Bayern Munich are wrong. Ribery says De Bruyne is not the right player for Pep Guardiola. Ribery says De Bruyne is different from Ribery and Arjen Robben. De Bruyne plays for Wolfsburg. He used to play for Chelsea. He has scored nine goals this year. He has 16 assists. This is the best in the league.

Kelsi Langley, the girlfriend of Arizona State University football player Davon Durant, has changed her story. She says she lied about being abused because of mood swings.

Durant was arrested for domestic violence after Langley said he hit her in the face and grabbed her neck during an argument in his car on March 7.

Langley was his girlfriend for 18 months.

Because of the arrest, Durant, who was a highly recruited player from a Kansas college, was suspended from the football team indefinitely and might be expelled from the university.

A young boy met his hero, Detroit Tigers pitcher Justin Verlander, at a Starbucks. The boy was wearing a dark blue shirt with Verlander’s name and jersey number, 35, on the back. Verlander took a selfie with the boy and posted the picture on his Instagram account.

Eden Hazard admitted that playing so many games for Chelsea and his national team this season may have left him too tired to play his best. He was taken off after 62 minutes in Belgium’s 1-0 win over Israel on Tuesday. Hazard has played 48 games this season for his club and his country, missing only five matches for Chelsea while helping them win the Premier League title. However, during Belgium’s difficult 1-0 victory over Israel in their European Championship qualifying group, manager Marc Wilmots substituted Hazard with 28 minutes left because he was having trouble beating his defender, Orel Dgani.

Police in the Northern Territory found 20 grams of marijuana hidden inside a leg of lamb. The meat was sent to a company at Darwin Airport and was likely headed to the Tiwi Islands, 100 kilometers to the north. The police noticed a strange smell, so they decided to x-ray the lamb, which showed the hidden bag of marijuana.

Former football player Clarke Carlisle has announced that he and his wife, Gemma, have separated. He has moved out of the house in Yorkshire where they lived together for 14 years. Carlisle is currently struggling with depression after a failed suicide attempt in December. This happened two days after he was arrested for suspected drunk driving. Gemma and Clarke are shown together in a photo from 213.

Paul Merson, a former Arsenal player, was forced to take back his comments after he criticized Andros Townsend’s call-up to the England team. and admitted he was wrong.

On Tuesday night in Turin, during a friendly match against Italy, Townsend came off the bench and scored a great goal to tie the game 1-1. This was a perfect response to Merson’s earlier criticism. Merson had written in his Sky Sports column that if Townsend was good enough for England, then anyone could be.

 Townsend celebrated his goal with his Tottenham teammates, Ryan Mason and Kyle Walker.

Cesc Fabregas, a midfielder for Chelsea, has a reputation for playing poorly in the second half of the season. He was one of the worst players in his team’s 2-0 loss to Holland on Tuesday. The 27-year-old was happy to play in southwest London earlier this week, but his performance has dropped significantly from his play around Christmas, when he looked like he would break the record for most assists in the Barclays Premier League.

West Midlands Police arrested six people in Dover this morning. They are suspected of terrorism offenses related to Syria.

The arrests happened around 8 a.m in the departure area of the port. Five men and one woman were taken into custody.

 Four of the men are in their 20s and live in Birmingham, in the West Midlands. The other two people are a 26-year-old man and a 23-year-old woman who do not have a fixed address.

 The six suspects are currently being questioned at a police station in the West Midlands.

People are likely to buy treats today at 12:52 pm. A study says that people in Britain spend an average of £62 a week on rewards. This includes buying things like chocolate, wine, expensive clothes, and shoes. The research was done by the website VoucherCodes.co.uk. Surprisingly, men spend a third more a month than women on treating themselves.

Arsene Wenger is very respected and known for being smart. When he speaks, people often agree with him. However, if you look closely at what he says, you might find that his ideas don’t have much solid proof. Usually, he talks about how Arsenal’s defense is actually statistically very good, even after their recent poor performance. But last week, he talked about a different issue: the idea of limiting the number of homegrown players in a Premier League team. Specifically, FA chairman Greg Dyke suggested increasing the number of homegrown players in a 25-player squad from eight to 12.

Charlie Austin said that his close friend Joey Barton ignored him on his first day at Queens Park Rangers, but Barton later realized his mistake. The two then became good friends. Austin had a memorable first season in the Premier League and is now considered a possible future England player after scoring 15 goals. His close friendship with club captain Barton is well known, but their first meeting is one Austin unlikely to forget.

This dog is his owner’s best friend because he saved him from a cold, muddy grave. The black dog was filmed bringing a rescue rope to his owner at the Clarence J. Brown Dam and Reservoir in Springfield, Ohio, on Saturday afternoon. The video shows the man, whose name is not disclosed, being pulled to shore by firefighters after spending nearly two hours in water that was around zero degrees. He apparently got stuck waist-deep in mud while trying to retrieve some duck hunting equipment. Luckily, he had a cell phone and called 911. However, first responders could not send a boat to him because the river was too shallow.

Juventus coach Massimiliano Allegri says he knows that the fans won’t fully support him until he wins them a championship. He joined Juventus last summer, a few months after being fired by AC Milan. Since then, he has done a great job, leading Juventus to the top of the Serie A standings. Allegri, who took over from Antonio Conte last summer, will try to win three more points this Saturday when Juventus plays Empoli at home.

Nathan Redmond scored the winning goal just six minutes into the match. Steven Whittaker passed the ball to him along the right side of the field. Redmond ran faster than defender Joe Bennett and crossed the ball into the box. Bradley Johnson hit the ball into the net from the back post. This goal won the game for his team at the Amex Stadium.

The residents of Celoron, New York, are upset about a statue of Lucille Ball, a famous comedian from their town. They have been unhappy with it for six years. The town opened the statue in 2009, but its face looks nothing like the real Lucille Ball. This has shocked and horrified the locals. The statue looks so bad that a Facebook page called "We Love Lucy! Get Rid of this Statue" has more than 660 likes. Some residents call the statue "monstous." The statue is based on a famous scene from her show "I Love Lucy," where she sells a health tonic while drunk.

South Sydney rugby league player Issac Luke, 27, is facing accusations of homophobia because of a offensive social media post he made in response to attacks from Canterbury Bulldogs fans. The player had previously posted a sincere message on his official Instagram account on Saturday, trying to find a young Rabbitohs fan who was allegedly attacked at ANZ Stadium in Sydney. Luke wanted to give the boy a jersey before the Easter long weekend as a way to make up for the incident that left the boy hospitalized after the controversial game.

People who are afraid of spiders, watch out. this story is scary. A man in Victoria, Australia, was shocked when a large huntsman spider came out from inside his car door handle. The video was recorded in Wangaratta, in northeast Victoria. It starts with the man walking up to his black Holden Ute and spraying insect repell on the door. The spray made the huntsman spider come out from under the door handle. The man said, "Get out, you bastard," in a calm voice. But when the hairy spider's legs came out, the man was not calm anymore. He yelled and moved back in fear.

Tottenham’s manager, Mauricio Pochettino, says that Harry Kane is like Gabriel Batistuta. Pochettino also said he will help Kane when things do not go well. Kane scored in his first game for England, just 79 seconds after he came on against Lithuania at Wembley on Friday night. This goal moved him to within two goals of scoring 30 goals this season. England’s manager, Roy Hodgson, wants to keep expectations for Kane low. Kane has risen quickly in his career, after finally joining the Tottenham first team, following loan spells at Leicester and Norwich. Mauricio Pochettino has compared Harry Kane to Gabriel Batistuta.

A former professional footballer, Michael McIndoe, who played for Bristol City and Wolverhampton Wanderers, is now struggling to survive on charity, a court was told. McIndoe ran a investment scheme that took in £33 million. He lived like a millionaire, partying in Marbella with attractive women and earning the nickname "Mr Big."

 He convinced other footballers to join the scheme by promising them a 20 20 percent return on their money. The scheme failed because of large debts. McIndoe was declared bankrupt last October with over £2 million in debt. Now, people he owes money to are taking him to court.

Pavel Nedved, a director at Juventus, said that Barcelona wants to sign Paul Pogba. Nedved told the newspaper Mundo Deportivo that Pogba will not be leaving Juventus. He also said he was happy that Juventus did not play against Barcelona in the Champions League quarter-finals.

James Oliver, 44, is a convicted sex offender. Linda Currier, 53, is his girlfriend. Police say she hit him with her car because she saw him trying to abuse a 12-year-old girl.

The incident happened on Saturday night in Noblesboro, Maine. Police found Oliver in the driveway of a home with a serious leg injury.

According to NBC News, Currier and Oliver argued inside the house. This argument started after Currier caught Oliver allegedly trying to sexually assault the young girl.

Brendan Rodgers, the manager of Liverpool, wants to sign a goalkeeper named Neto from Fiorentina. But he has strong competition for him. PSG and several Spanish clubs also want Neto. This is what Neto’s agent, Stefano Castagna, says.

The 25-year-old Neto’s contract with Fiorentina ends in June. Earlier this season, Liverpool was interested in signing him. This happened after their current goalkeeper, Simon Mignolet, was removed from the team.

In January, Liverpool tried to sign Neto, but the deal did not happen. Now, it seems very likely that Neto will leave Fiorentina in the summer.

A video by YouTuber Richard Stewart shows a Porsche Cayman losing control on Prince Edward Island, Canada. The car speeds away from a green light, swerves wildly, and crashes into a concrete median. One wheel comes off before the car stops. Stewart wrote on YouTube, "Just because you have a nice car doesn't make you a good driver. Don't let your son drive your Porsche!"

This weekend, Sportsmail will provide information for every Premier League game, including team news, possible lineups, betting odds, and statistics from Opta. Here is the information for Sunderland’s home game against Newcastle at the Stadium of Light.

 Sunderland: Midfielder Lee Cattermole will start the game against Newcastle on Sunday. Manager Dick Advocaat confirmed that Cattermole is back after serving a two-game ban for getting 10 yellow cards this season.

If Rory McIlroy wins the upcoming Masters, it will make him the first gol ever to win all four major championships, a career grand slam. This would finish a lifelong dream for the world’s top golfer. To mark the moment, McIlroy and his sponsor Bose made a video showing his life story—from playing on small practice greens as a child to becoming a golf star, including some tough times. The video starts with McIlroy going for a morning run, with the words “Six weeks to Georgia” on the screen. It also includes an interview with McIlroy when he was young, before he became famous.

Sergio Garcia says he is only thinking about winning his first PGA Tour event since 2022 at this week’s Shell Houston Open. The Masters tournament is coming up soon, but he is not distracted by it. Rory McIlroy is trying to win three majors in a row to complete his career grand slam. and people are wondering if Tiger Woods will return to golf after staying away for a while. These questions have been the main news for weeks. The Golf Club of Houston is set up to try to copy some of the conditions at Augusta, but Garcia is focused on ending his long wait for a win. Sergio Garcia was seen lining up a putt at the Cadillac Championship in Doral, Florida last month.

Riki Hughes, a 31-year-old Iraq war veteran, went to jail for 16 months. He stole £17,000 from a children's football club where he volunteered as the club secretary.

He took the money from the Tidworth Town Football Club's accounts. He told people he was paying rent to the club's landlord, even though the team was using the building for free.

 Instead, he spent the money on himself. This included buying camping gear and going on a stag (bachelor) holiday to Las Vegas.

Johnny Sexton is used to winning. He has won many gold medals and now he is trying to keep winning. He is getting ready for a big game on Sunday in Paris against Saracens. This game is part of the European Champions Cup.

 Sexton plays number 10 for Racing Metro and is also famous for playing for Ireland. He said he has been lucky to play for good teams with Leinster and Ireland. He has won trophies almost every year. The 29-year-old has been a senior player since 22. The only year since then that he did not win a big prize was 2010.

Mustafa Kamal stepped down as president of the International Cricket Council (ICC) on Wednesday. He accused India of influencing the result of the Cricket World Cup quarter-final match between Bangladesh and India.

 Kamal, who is from Bangladesh, made these accusations at the airport after returning from the tournament in Australia. He said, "Everyone saw what happened during the Bangladesh-India match. India used its position in the ICC to influence the outcome of the match."

 He added, "From now on, I am a former president of the ICC. I would have reacted the same way if this had happened to any other country."

West Ham manager Sam Allardyce supports Nigel Pearson, the manager of Leicester City. Allardyce thinks highly of Pearson for being independent and doing what he believes is right. Allardyce worked with Pearson at Newcastle United in 207 when Allardyce was the manager. The two will work together again when West Ham plays Leicester at the King Power Stadium on Saturday. Pearson has been involved in several controversial incidents this season, including grabbing Crystal Palace's James McArthur by the throat and losing his cool with a reporter during a press conference. Leicester City boss Nigel Pearson (left) has been involved in a number of controversial incidents this season .

Sunderland’s manager, John O'Shea, told his team to take control of their own destiny by beating Newcastle for a fifth consecutive derby win. The two teams play at the Stadium of Light on Sunday. Sunderland has won the last four games against Newcastle, but they desperately need three points to stay safe in the Premier League. O'Shea and his players could end up in the releg zone if Burnley beats Tottenham in the earlier game that day. That would make getting three points very important.

Stoke City manager Mark Hughes believes his team should finally win a game at Chelsea’s stadium, Stamford Bridge. Since Stoke was promoted to the Premier League in 288, they have played Chelsea away eight times in all competitions and lost every time. The last time Stoke won at Chelsea was in 1995, when they won the League Cup. Since a 1-1 tie in 1984, Stoke has not earned a single point in any match at Chelsea’s home ground. Hughes says his team must end this losing streak. Frank Lampard, pictured celebrating after Chelsea’s 3-0 win over Stoke, represents their most recent visit to Stamford Bridge.

Newcastle United wants to avoid losing their third game in a row when they play their rivals, Sunderland, this Sunday. They have been playing badly in recent weeks without their striker, Papiss Cisse, who is banned. Dug, a pug, has recovered after being bitten in the face by a rattlesnake. Dug and his owner, Lindsay Castro, were hiking on the Jurupa Hills trail in Fontana, Canada, on Thursday. Although Rodgers tried to stay positive, he did not hide the fact that this has been a tough season. Many fans want to buy rare items that used to belong to their favorite players or teams. because these small pieces of history can sell for thousands of pounds. People have seen images of Jesus on toast, pancakes, crisps, and ice cream. But a builder was surprised when he saw an image of Jesus on a piece of wood just before Easter. Paddy Morrall, a 31-year-old builder from Keighley near Bradford, saw the full-length image of Christ on a broken scaffolding board in Inverness, Scotland, on Wednesday. The image of Jesus wearing a robe appeared after the wood was left out in the rain for several hours. Paddy has kept the board.

On Tuesday, Slovakia beat the Czech Republic 1-0 in a friendly soccer match. Ondrej Duda scored the only goal after halftime. The 20-year-old midfielder kicked a low shot from outside the penalty area in the 49th minute. It was his second goal for his national team. This was Slovakia's third win in 10 games against the Czech Republic since the two countries split in 1993. The Czech Republic has won five of those games. During the match, Slovakia's Martin Skrtel hit Czech player Daniel Kolar in the face with a high kick. Slovakia’s win continued their strong recent performance.

People in Shandong Province, China, have been carrying natural gas in plastic bags. Recent photos show people from Lijin village in Dongying city putting the gas into bags that can be up to six meters long and pushing them on rickshaws. People’s Daily Online reported this. People who saw this were worried because it is like carrying a bomb. If the bags touched fire or even a cigarette, it could cause a big disaster. Gas-guzzler: Caring natural gas in huge plastic bags is a common scene in some villages in Shandong. Penny-pinching: Local media suggest this is a way for villages to save money on the transportation of gas.

Tiger Woods was seen practicing at Augusta National, which gives fans hope that he will play in this year’s Masters. The Masters is the first major tournament of the year. However, even though Celtic won, the match showed that they will have to work hard to keep winning the league title. The game was played on a Friday night.

Ulster has signed Charles Piutau, a player from New Zealand. Piutau can play as a full back, winger, or center. He has agreed to play for Ulster for two years, starting in July 2016.  In another game, Miralem Pjanic scored the only goal to help AS Roma beat Napoli 1-1. This was Roma's first home win in over four months.

Northampton rugby team says that George North, a player for Wales, will not play in Saturday’s big game against Clermont Auvergne. This is because he hurt his head again. North was lying still on the field after being knocked out during the game against Wasps. Mallinder said it was a bad hit, and North was unconscious for a short time.

Cesar Azpilicueta, a defender for Chelsea, believes his team will win the Barclays Premier League. He says they have shown their strength by staying at the top of the league since the beginning of the season.

Mohamed Diame will return to play for Hull City when they visit Swansea on Saturday. Hull’s manager, Steve Bruce, said that Diame will play for part of the game. Bruce said, “He will play. A group of U.S. senators wrote to FIFA, the world governing body for football, asking them to take the 2028 World Cup away from Russia. The senators said this should happen because of Russia's involvement in the Ukraine crisis and its takeover of Crimea. The letter, was dated Tuesday and made public on Wednesday. It was signed by 13 lawmakers from both the Democratic and Republican parties, who strongly urged FIFA to move the tournament to a different location.

Arango, who is 44 years old, said, "I did something I shouldn't have done with Zavala."
